name: Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport
before:
Alaska's main airport, five miles south west of downtown Anchorage, and one of the busiest cargo airports in the world thanks to its position on the trans-Pacific routes.

For a client it is also the gateway to everything else in the state. Every regional intrastate carrier uses the South Terminal, alongside Alaska Airlines, Delta, American, United, Air Canada, Sun Country and the German carriers Condor and Discover. The South Terminal has 24 gates across three concourses and the North Terminal another eight.

The detail worth telling a client: right next door is the Lake Hood Seaplane Base, the busiest seaplane base in the world, from which floatplanes leave for the bush.

The airport covers 4,608 acres with three runways, the longest at 12,400 feet, and handles around 718 movements a day. Roughly a third of that is scheduled airline flying and the rest is general aviation and air taxi work.

It is named after Ted Stevens, who served as a senator for Alaska from 1968 to 2009.
after:
Alaska's main airport, five miles south west of downtown Anchorage, and in 2025 the third busiest cargo airport in the world, thanks to its position on the trans-Pacific routes.

For a client it is also the main starting point for flights around Alaska. The South Terminal has three concourses, A, B and C, while US customs is in the North Terminal. Among its airlines, the airport lists Alaska Airlines, American, Delta, Hawaiian, Sun Country and United, with Air Canada, Condor and WestJet from abroad.

The detail worth telling a client: right next door is the Lake Hood Seaplane Base, the busiest seaplane base in the world.

Of the airport's three runways, the longest is 12,400 feet. The airport is named after Ted Stevens, who served as a senator for Alaska from 1968 to 2009.

The operator's older pages give fourth (airline page, January 2026 handbook) and fifth (About page), earlier years' ranks. The FAA's preliminary CY2025 table puts Anchorage first in the US for all-cargo landed weight; that US rank is not added, because on ACI's measure excluding transit Louisville says it led North America in 2025 (see the Louisville ledger).

claims.note: Replaces 'alongside Alaska Airlines, Delta, American, United, Air Canada, Sun Country and the German carriers Condor and Discover' (Wikipedia). The operator's live list, which it says it updates periodically, has no Discover (Wikipedia still lists it), adds Hawaiian and WestJet, and names three smaller Alaskan carriers (Aleutian Airways, Grant Aviation, Ravn Alaska) not repeated here. It does not list Southwest, which Wikipedia says began seasonal flights from Denver and Las Vegas on 15 May 2026; that is not confirmed, so Southwest is not named. BTS's carrier shares for July 2025 to June 2026 bear out the four big US airlines (Alaska 63.05 per cent, Delta 13.46, United 7.25, American 3.71).
